subject: Time series data not continuous but with a pattern

messages.author: 7374fce48170779f
messages.subject: Time series data not continuous but with a pattern
parts:
Dear all,

I am building a spatio-temporal model using a dataset that does not have a continuous time series but with a pattern, the data was collected in the same 8 continuous time periods every day for 30 days, half an hour for a time period, so the last period of one day should not be temporally correlated with the first time period in the next day, this got me wondering: 

1. Is there a way to tell the model to separate when it comes to a new day? 
2. Is it helpful to set up another index column in the dataset to group each day, and let it be independent with each other, for example,
    
          f(ID.groupbyday, model="iid"),

    and add this to the formula? The formula I'm using is (assuming a type II interaction):

          formula<- y ~ 1 + f(ID.loc, model="besag", graph=tp.adj) +
                                      f(ID.time, model="ar1") + 
                                      f(ID.time1, model="iid") +
                                      f(ID.loc.int, model="iid", group=ID.time.int, control.group=list(model="ar1"))

Do you know how to deal with this problem?

Thanks a lot!

Chris

Sorry for not being clear, let me rephrase. As described at the beginning, here is an example of my dataset, let's say the observation only took place at two time periods a day at two different stations separately, the data are organized as shown in the figure: 

You can see that time period 2 and 3 has a time span of 22 hours, which is not continuous, while time period 1 and 2 are continuous, and so does time period 3 and 4, but there is a pattern in it because for time period 4 and 5 (not shown in the figure), there is also a 22-hour span in between and so on. 


I think this is a problem for temporal effect modeling, right?


So, my question is that given the sample dataset described above, how to deal with this pattern when modeling the temporal effect using INLA?


The two points that I specified in the first post are the ideas that I think may be useful for handling this problem.


Thanks again!

Best!

Chris
